newsitem.title: GERMANY: PKK leader promises no more violence in Germany.
newsitem.headline: PKK leader promises no more violence in Germany.

text.p: The leader of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) was quoted on Tuesday as saying the militant organisation would carry out no more violent attacks in Germany.

"I will take responsibility for the fact that Kurds living in Germany will behave better than other nationalities... even better than German society," ZDF television quoted Abdullah Ocalan as saying in an interview.
"They will behave in accordance with the law. I guarantee that," Ocalan said, according to written extracts of the interview released ahead of broadcast on Wednesday evening.

Bonn banned the PKK after a spectacular spate of attacks across Germany and other European countries in 1993. Officials say PKK-sponsored violence appears to have declined in Germany over the past year or so.
The PKK has mounted a bloody guerrilla campaign for Kurdish self-rule in Turkey since 1984, in which many thousands have been killed.

In contrast to previous pledges to renounce violence in Germany, ZDF said Ocalan had told them his latest promise was unconditional and not llimited in time. He also said German tourists in Turkey need not fear attacks.

Ocalan is one of Turkey's most wanted men. He has been reported to be living in the Syrian-controlled Bekaa Valley in Lebanon. ZDF said it had interviewed him at a PKK camp close to the Syrian capital Damascus.
